static_analysis_justification:
The project applies multiple FLOSS static analysis tools as a merge gate on every proposed change, and releases are cut only from green CI:
 - Clippy (FLOSS) runs via the clippy job in .github/workflows/ci.yml as cargo clippy --locked --all-targets --features test-helpers -- -D warnings, with strict pedantic lint rules enabled project-wide ([lints.clippy] in Cargo.toml; unwrap_used denied). Warnings fail the build.
 - SonarCloud (SonarQube, listed by this criterion as an example tool) scans the repo on pushes to main and non-fork PRs via the sonarqube job (SonarSource/sonarqube-scan-action), configured in sonar-project.properties.
 - Shell scripts (install.sh) are analyzed with shellcheck and PowerShell scripts with PSScriptAnalyzer in the same workflow.
Since CI must be green before a release branch/tag is cut, these tools are applied to every major release.
static_analysis_common_vulnerabilities_j:
Two of the applied tools look for common vulnerabilities:
 - SonarCloud/SonarQube applies security-focused rulesets including taint analysis to the scanned code.
 - cargo-deny (.github/workflows/dependency-policy.yml, cargo deny check on every push and PR) checks all dependencies against the RustSec Advisory Database, detecting known vulnerabilities in the crates the software is built on.
static_analysis_fixed_justification: Project policy: confirmed medium-or-higher severity vulnerabilities found by static analysis or dependency auditing (cargo-deny/RustSec, SonarCloud, Dependabot) are fixed in a timely way, well within the 60-day window required by vulnerabilities_60_days. Enforcement is structural: Clippy runs with -D warnings and cargo-deny fails CI on advisories at the configured severity, so no release can be cut while a flagged issue is unresolved — fixing it is the only path to a green build. No confirmed medium+ static-analysis vulnerabilities are currently outstanding.
static_analysis_often_justification: Static analysis runs on essentially every commit: both workflows trigger on: push to main and on: pull_request to main. The Clippy job runs unconditionally on every event (including forked and Dependabot PRs — noted explicitly in the workflow as the SAST backstop), and SonarCloud scans every push to main.
report_responses_justification: Every bug report filed in the last 2-12 months has been acknowledged on the public tracker (response need not include a fix); see https://github.com/randomparity/bzr/issues — recent reports such as #504, #505, #512 were triaged and driven to merged fixes or explicit dispositions.
enhancement_responses_justification: Enhancement requests in the last 2-12 months (e.g. #457-#482) each received a response — discussion, triage, or implementation — on the public issue tracker.
report_archive_justification: GitHub Issues provides a searchable, URL-addressable public archive of all reports and responses: https://github.com/randomparity/bzr/issues
vulnerability_report_process_justificati: SECURITY.md at the repository root publishes the vulnerability reporting process: do not open a public issue; email randomparity@gmail.com with description, reproduction steps, and affected versions; acknowledgment within 72 hours; fixes developed privately and released as patch versions. GitHub Security Advisories are named as the canonical public inventory.
vulnerability_report_private_justificati: Private reports are supported two ways, both documented in SECURITY.md: direct email to randomparity@gmail.com and GitHub's private vulnerability reporting (https://github.com/randomparity/bzr/security/advisories).
vulnerability_report_response_justificat: No vulnerability reports have been received in the last 6 months, so there is no initial response time to evaluate.
build_floss_tools_justification: The project builds with FLOSS tools only: rustc/cargo and GNU make (Makefile). No proprietary build tools are used.
test_justification: An automated three-tier test suite ships in the repository: unit tests in sibling *_tests.rs files, HTTP-mocked integration tests using wiremock (tests/integration.rs), and functional tests running the real binary against Bugzilla containers (tests/functional/). How to run the suites is documented in CONTRIBUTING.md and the Makefile (make test, make functional-test-all).
test_invocation_justification: Standard invocation for the language: cargo test (wrapped by make test for quieter output).
test_most_justification: The suite covers most functionality: command dispatch, CLI parsing, query/filter construction, REST/XML-RPC transport incl. hybrid fallback and retry logic, config handling, output formatting, and error paths, verified at three tiers including live-server functional tests. Coverage is measured via cargo-llvm-cov in the SonarCloud job (.github/workflows/ci.yml).
test_continuous_integration_justificatio: CI (.github/workflows/ci.yml) builds and runs the automated test suite on every push to main and every pull_request.
test_policy_justification: CONTRIBUTING.md states the policy: "Add tests for changed behavior, including error and edge paths. User-facing CLI changes also require coverage in tests/functional/phases/ against a real Bugzilla container."
tests_are_added_justification: Recent major changes adhere to the policy: new functionality lands with unit tests plus functional phase scripts under tests/functional/phases/ (the repo's contribution rules treat a missing functional test as an incomplete change), and the check-test-layout CI job enforces the test layout.
tests_documented_added_justification: The test-adding policy is documented in the contribution instructions (CONTRIBUTING.md, lines around "Add tests for changed behavior").
warnings_justification: Compiler warnings plus the clippy linter are enabled and enforced: CI runs cargo clippy --locked --all-targets -- -D warnings (.github/workflows/ci.yml, clippy job).
warnings_fixed_justification: Warnings are addressed structurally: clippy runs with -D warnings so any warning fails CI; the tree is warning-free.
warnings_strict_justification: Maximally strict: [lints.clippy] in Cargo.toml enables pedantic lints, denies unwrap_used, and treats warnings as errors; the pre-commit hook also runs fmt --check and clippy.
know_secure_design_justification: The primary developer applies secure design principles in the codebase: TLS certificate pinning with TOFU first-use capture and issuer-change detection (src/tls/), deny-by-default trust policy, least-privilege credential handling via OS keyrings, API-key redaction across logs/errors, and input validation via allowlists (src/validation/).
know_common_errors_justification: Common vulnerability classes are known and mitigated concretely: credential leakage (redaction seams, fixed across issues #505, #509, #511, #512), template/injection risks in release workflows (issue #525), unbounded input retention (issue #512 bounding HttpStatus.body), and TOFU pin mismatches surfaced as distinct errors (PinMismatch, IssuedChanged in src/error.rs).
crypto_published_justification: Only publicly published and expert-reviewed cryptography is used: TLS via rustls and SHA-256 via the sha2 crate for certificate pinning. No custom algorithms.
crypto_call_justification: bzr does not re-implement cryptography; it calls dedicated implementations: rustls (via reqwest, Cargo.toml features rustls-tls-native-roots) for TLS and sha2 for hashing.
crypto_floss_justification: All cryptographic functionality uses FLOSS components: rustls, sha2, rustls-native-certs, webpki-roots (Apache-2.0/MIT licensed crates).
crypto_keylength_justification: rustls enforces NIST-minimum key lengths by default and cannot be configured below them; certificate pins use SHA-256 (224+ bit). No smaller keylengths are configurable.
crypto_working_justification: Defaults use no broken algorithms: rustls supports only modern TLS with AEAD cipher suites; the codebase contains no MD5/SHA-1/RC4/single-DES usage (fingerprint.rs formats SHA-256 pins).
crypto_weaknesses_justification: No known-serious weak primitives are depended on: no SHA-1 (TOFU pins are SHA-256), rustls disables TLS below 1.2 by default, and there is no SSH/CBC usage.
crypto_pfs_justification: TLS connections via rustls use (E)DHE key exchange, providing perfect forward secrecy for all session keys.
crypto_password_storage_justification: bzr performs outbound authentication only: it stores Bugzilla API keys/tokens in the OS keyring. It does not authenticate external users with passwords, so no inbound password storage exists.
crypto_random_justification: bzr does not generate cryptographic keys or nonces itself; all key establishment and randomness is delegated to rustls and the operating system TLS stack.
delivery_unsigned_justification: install.sh retrieves all content over HTTPS from github.com; no cryptographic hashes are fetched over plain HTTP without signature verification.
vulnerabilities_fixed_60_days_justificat: There are no unpatched vulnerabilities of medium or higher severity that have been publicly known for more than 60 days. SECURITY.md commits to fixing vulnerabilities on the latest stable minor release line and publishing GitHub Security Advisories with first-fixed-version guidance.
vulnerabilities_critical_fixed_justifica: No critical vulnerabilities are currently known. SECURITY.md's process (private fix development, prompt patch release, 72-hour acknowledgment) is designed to fix critical vulnerabilities rapidly after they are reported.
no_leaked_credentials_justification: The repository contains no valid private credentials: bzr resolves credentials at runtime from OS keyrings, environment-backed sources, or user config outside the repo (src/credentials/); CI examples use throwaway keychains; and secret scanning runs in the supply-chain toolchain.
dynamic_analysis_unsafe_justification: bzr is written entirely in Rust, a memory-safe language; the project produces no C or C++ code.
dynamic_analysis_enable_assertions_justi: Fuzzing and testing build in debug configuration, so Rust debug_assertions are enabled during dynamic analysis (cargo fuzz run compiles dev-profile binaries; assertions are not forced into release builds).
dynamic_analysis_fixed_justification: Any medium-or-higher severity vulnerabilities discovered by fuzzing will be fixed promptly after confirmation, consistent with the static-analysis and disclosure policies in SECURITY.md; none have been confirmed to date.
